To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the vast majority of whiplash associated disorder patients recover within three months and that early return to normal activities, self exercise and manual therapy are beneficial, and collars, rest and negative attitudes and behaviour are detrimental.

whiplash associated injuries are common, but physical serious injuries are rare; the majority of patients with whiplash associated disorder will recover within 3 months; recovery is improved if patients return to normal activities as soon as they are able, and if they are encouraged to self-manage and self-exercise; recovery is delayed if patients are given collars, advised to rest, or told that the prognosis is poor; and, the prognosis is improved by patients' having a positive attitude, and
whiplash associated disorder is a self limiting condition with a good prognosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving outcomes for whiplash associated disorder patients, by providing evidence based patient information and advice.
the provision of information and advice to patients in a manner that is both evidence based and patient centred.
the dissemination of evidence based information to patients and the public.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the majority of people with whiplash associated disorder recover fully, and that early return to normal activities, self exercise and manual therapy are helpful, while collars, rest and negative attitudes and behaviours are not.

the evidence supports a return to normal pre-injury activities, self management and exercise, manual therapy, and reassurance about good outcome, while collars, rest and negative attitudes and behaviours delay recovery.
whiplash associated disorder is a self limiting condition with an excellent prognosis, and the best advice is to get active as soon as possible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best approach to whiplash associated disorder is to encourage a positive attitude and early return to normal activities, and avoid over-medicalisation, collars, rest and negative beliefs.
the evidence supports a patient centred approach that includes early mobilisation, exercise, and manual treatment.

the evidence supports the provision of patient centred information to whiplash patients that is consistent with the evidence, and is based on the following principles: (i) reassurance about prognosis, (ii) avoidance of over-medicalisation, (iii) avoidance of rest and collar use, (iv) encouragement of normal activities, (v) encouragement of exercise, and (vi) avoidance of negative attitudes and beliefs.
